scope: Targeted primary-source criticism supporting the authorized cable/connector cycle. This is literature and source inspection, with no simulator runs or learned-performance evidence.

decision.simplest_credible_baseline: Force-controlled approach, bounded probe/depart grid or spiral search, insertion and retract/retry; precontact wrench compensation; add a visible-snag lift/arc rule only after its geometric feasibility is demonstrated.
decision.practical_reference: Run the AIC ground-truth CheatCode reference for engineering only, then the force-guided baseline with the project's declared observations. WaveArm is an API example. RunACT is an externally hosted proof of concept whose model license and usable checkpoint were not verified here.
decision.smallest_research_question: On physically witnessed insertion failures with a retained prior clip/connection, do action-conditioned predictions of both local engagement and distal constraint loss improve complete-job recovery over the strongest affordable compensation, rule and cable-planning alternatives at matched experience?
decision.novelty_boundary: Cable-aware control, load compensation, learned corrective skills, memory, graph dynamics, predicted wrench, and preserving assembly relations already exist. Their combination is a hypothesis to test, not an established original contribution.
decision.reject_or_revise_if: If compensation or visible-snag rules solve the balanced local-error by snag factorial equally well, reject a learned reliability benefit. If bad repair consequences cannot be predicted on held-out actions, revise the predictor before control training.
candidate_evidence_needed: A common competent first attempt producing feasible witnessed failures.
Prediction accuracy for progress, load and prior-constraint loss on held-out good and bad repairs.
Matched-observation control comparisons and whole-job denominators, including initial successes and all aborts.
Held-out layout/mechanical combinations; connector transfer only with separate geometry holdout.

pinned_upstream.pin_source: Parent agent supplied cloned HEAD; claims below were checked in that local checkout.

benchmark_claim_matrix.verified: UR5e qualification is single insertion of a pregrasped SFP or SC plug; the other end remains free. Known plug/port types and the same cable are used. Robot starts near the target; board/component placements vary. Official evaluation uses Gazebo without Flowstate.
benchmark_claim_matrix.limits: No pickup, routing, previously completed clip/connection retention, or unseen connector geometry claim follows.
benchmark_claim_matrix.implication: Version the connected-end/clip/snag task as a project extension and keep official scores separate.

benchmark_claim_matrix.access: Full pinned local scoring documentation; implementation not audited by this review.
benchmark_claim_matrix.verified: Scoring awards contact-sensor full insertion, separate partial/proximity credit, motion quality and time points. The documented force penalty is minus 12 points for a startup-tared reading above 20 N for longer than one second.
benchmark_claim_matrix.limits: This is not the retired project's instantaneous raw 20 N abort, and the score is not a binary complete-job success rate or an electrical/optical functionality test.
benchmark_claim_matrix.implication: Register seating/retention/dwell and project hard limits explicitly; preserve official scoring separately.

benchmark_claim_matrix.access: Official web README plus full pinned local example README and relevant Isaac config lines.
benchmark_claim_matrix.verified: Documented official stack is ROS 2 Kilted with containers or Ubuntu 24.04. CheatCode uses simulator TF truth unavailable in official evaluation. WaveArm does not attempt insertion. RunACT references a small-data external ACT policy. Isaac config has end-effector pose commands/rewards, timeout termination, disabled robot contact sensors and no gripper action.
benchmark_claim_matrix.limits: The Isaac training command does not establish a completed insertion environment. Native Windows official-evaluator readiness is unverified.
benchmark_claim_matrix.implication: Use references with truthful controller/observation labels. Runtime implementation must supply physical engagement and contact checks before comparison.

benchmark_claim_matrix.access: Full pinned local README; script hashed; this review does not claim exhaustive script verification.
benchmark_claim_matrix.verified: Documented conversion needs exported Gazebo SDF, SDFormat/Gazebo Python bindings and generated mesh files. Postprocessing configures the cable plugin, actuators and FT sensors, modifies inertias, lifts a cable end, adds a gripper weld and excludes SC-port/SC-plug contact.
benchmark_claim_matrix.limits: An available MJCF mirror is not demonstrated physics parity or validated insertion. README weld names reference an LC plug.
benchmark_claim_matrix.implication: Audit exact port collisions, attachment and success before using converted geometry. Keep source unchanged and implement corrections in versioned adapters.

literature_claim_matrix.title: Cable Routing and Assembly using Tactile-driven Motion Primitives
literature_claim_matrix.access: Full HTML; methods IV and experiments V inspected.
literature_claim_matrix.established: Vision parses the board; tactile state machines follow, pivot, weave and insert. Insertion uses force-maintaining rotary exploration and retreat/resampled retries. Tension is controlled. Reported 48/50 isolated insertions and 51/60 complete jobs are separate evaluations; complete-job failures include four connector failures, three stuck cables and two losses of prior fixtures.
literature_claim_matrix.limitation_or_distinction: Their discussion explicitly identifies global cable changes insufficiently captured by local tactile sensing. This motivates global-state measurements but does not establish that a predictive model outperforms global vision/force rules.
literature_claim_matrix.baseline_implication: Use contact-guided exploration/retry plus visible cable-state correction; do not compare only with blind straight insertion.

literature_claim_matrix.title: Multi-Stage Cable Routing through Hierarchical Imitation Learning
literature_claim_matrix.access: Full HTML; low-level demonstrations, high-level policy and experiments inspected.
literature_claim_matrix.established: The clip skill learns from 1442 demonstrations including roughly 600 recovery examples. A learned high-level controller selects primitives including cable perturbation and uses history. The paper reports 12/24 three-clip success and a zero-success memoryless ablation; recovery demonstrations, corrective skill selection and memory already exist.
literature_claim_matrix.limitation_or_distinction: The task routes a cable through clips; it is not evidence for this project's connector-after-snag assay. Above 95% of their failures are attributed to premature go_next decisions under ambiguous routing perception.
literature_claim_matrix.baseline_implication: Include a competent history-bearing learned baseline when learning is justified. Do not remove available global observations to manufacture ambiguity.

literature_claim_matrix.title: AI-based Framework for Robust Model-Based Connector Mating in Robotic Wire Harness Installation
literature_claim_matrix.access: Full HTML; methods III, experiments IV and results V inspected.
literature_claim_matrix.established: Force-controlled approach/contact/depart probe search is optimized through learned, environment-conditioned trajectory and wrench models. Five automotive connectors with adapted gripping ribs are studied; roughly 4000 executions per connector supply data. Table III reports improved success/time on 100 unseen in-distribution cases per connector.
literature_claim_matrix.limitation_or_distinction: Predicting insertion outcomes/wrenches to optimize actions is already demonstrated. The inspected experiment is local mating; it does not establish the proposed combined snag/prior-constraint comparison. AIC connector geometry and grasping differ.
literature_claim_matrix.baseline_implication: Use force-controlled search as a strong baseline. Test the added distal consequence prediction against local-only prediction with otherwise comparable inputs/capacity.

literature_claim_matrix.title: Force Guided Assembly Under Bias
literature_claim_matrix.access: Institutional abstract and full thesis PDF; chapter 7 cable-model assumptions, identification and experimental setup inspected.
literature_claim_matrix.established: Precontact modeling separates hose/cable bias from connector contact. Cable experiments identify axial/flexural spring and local correction models by least squares from translation/rotation motions.
literature_claim_matrix.limitation_or_distinction: Chapter 7 assumes a taut approximately straight cable, negligible gravity-induced curvature/torsion/hysteresis, and planar experiments. Compensating cable loads is old; changing contact topology may invalidate a locally identified bias model but that failure must be measured here.
literature_claim_matrix.baseline_implication: Start with constant precontact tare and a small affine/local wrench model where justified. Keep uncompensated total load available for project limits.

literature_claim_matrix.title: Feel the Tension: Manipulation of Deformable Linear Objects in Environments with Fixtures using Force Information
literature_claim_matrix.access: Full HTML; representation IV, estimation V, control VI and experimental scope inspected.
literature_claim_matrix.established: An online reduced contact graph estimates contact locations, elasticity and tension, supporting clipping/sliding/winding primitives and a dual-arm YuMi harness-production demonstration. It accounts for prior configuration when updating global state.
literature_claim_matrix.limitation_or_distinction: The model relies on tensioned nearly straight segments and controlled grasp/sliding. Sequence planning is explicitly outside its scope. Graph state, force inference and diagnostic motions are already established.
literature_claim_matrix.baseline_implication: A compact contact/length/tension model may be sufficient; compare it before adding graph neural dynamics.

literature_claim_matrix.title: Real-time Contact State Estimation in Shape Control of Deformable Linear Objects under Small Environmental Constraints
literature_claim_matrix.access: Full HTML; contact indicators IV, adaptive control V and experiment setup VI inspected.
literature_claim_matrix.established: Indicators based on detected versus applied force detect contact establishment/change. A clip-state sequence detects anomalies, updates motion-height/force parameter ranges and retries. Experiments use two Franka Panda arms.
literature_claim_matrix.limitation_or_distinction: Contact anomaly detection and feedback correction already exist. These clip-force semantics depend on tautness/quasistatic staging and should not be copied as universal insertion predicates.
literature_claim_matrix.baseline_implication: Measure force-response/stall indicators and use simple state-based corrective rules before attributing benefit to learning.

literature_claim_matrix.title: Robotic Cable Routing with Spatial Representation
literature_claim_matrix.access: Author project methods page and linked code directory inspected; complete planner implementation and its license not audited.
literature_claim_matrix.established: A graph planner tracks cable/fixture side relations and uses learned stretch/cross/insert primitives. RGB-D estimates the spatial representation. The author page shows overstretching and slack failure cases.
literature_claim_matrix.limitation_or_distinction: Cable-environment graphs and planning to preserve route relations are established. The visible linked code directory alone does not prove the complete planner is ready to reuse.
literature_claim_matrix.baseline_implication: Implement a clearly labeled simplified spatial-relation planner with the same insertion controller if direct reproduction is unavailable.

literature_claim_matrix.title: Learning Graph Dynamics With External Contact for Deformable Linear Objects Shape Control
literature_claim_matrix.access: Primary publisher abstract returned by search. Direct full-page access hit a JavaScript verification page; full methods/experiments were not read.
literature_claim_matrix.established: The abstract describes graph-convolution dynamics over cable/contact-object keypoints and scoring sampled actions by predicted shape progress, with six simulation scenarios and physical tests.
literature_claim_matrix.limitation_or_distinction: Action-conditioned cable/contact prediction and sampled-action selection already exist. No absence of connector/retention capability is inferred from inaccessible full text.
literature_claim_matrix.baseline_implication: Treat graph dynamics itself as prior art. The candidate must earn a measured task-specific consequence/control distinction.

literature_claim_matrix.title: Wiring connector-terminated cables based on manipulation planning with collision-free EMD net
literature_claim_matrix.access: Publisher abstract/highlights via search; direct publisher page returned 403. Original paper PDF was available from an institutional repository; abstract/introduction checked, detailed results not audited.
literature_claim_matrix.established: A learned Encode-Manipulate-Decode model predicts shape changes while transporting a grasped connector and plans cable-collision-avoiding trajectories. The paper's stated goal is delivery near the socket and compatibility with separate insertion methods.
literature_claim_matrix.limitation_or_distinction: Predicting distal cable effects of connector motion is established. The access depth does not support claims about absent recovery or constraint-retention experiments.
literature_claim_matrix.baseline_implication: A cable-aware transport planner followed by identical force insertion directly challenges the need for joint local/distal repair prediction.

literature_claim_matrix.title: A Graph-based framework for assembly sequence planning of a cable harness
literature_claim_matrix.access: Primary publisher abstract, introduction and section snippets via search; complete method text unavailable in this review.
literature_claim_matrix.established: Assembly representation includes already assembled relations along the cable; feasible sequences account for topology, task types and sequence-sensitive constraints for non-looped single/multibranch harnesses.
literature_claim_matrix.limitation_or_distinction: Representing completed assembly relations and their effect on future feasibility is prior art. No omission of dynamic recovery is inferred from limited access.
literature_claim_matrix.baseline_implication: Make loss of prior relations an explicit invariant and measured failure, not an assumed novel representation.

literature_claim_matrix.title: SILO: Simulation-in-the-Loop Sim-to-Real Transfer for Multi-Stage Cable Routing
literature_claim_matrix.access: Full HTML; training/state construction, deployment and main experiments inspected.
literature_claim_matrix.established: State-based RL routes through a local harness using nearby cable points and robot state; grasp/move primitives compose multiple stages. Deployment synchronizes a simulated robot and uses simulated action outcomes as real joint targets; cable observations come from perception.
literature_claim_matrix.limitation_or_distinction: Reactive simulated cable learning and hardware routing already exist. Their paper explicitly cautions that historical h-IL comparisons differ in assumptions and cycle time is estimated from videos. Those results cannot be imported as our baselines.
literature_claim_matrix.baseline_implication: Use substantive learning only after local task validation and measure fresh task throughput. Do not claim sim-to-real from simulation.

literature_claim_matrix.title: WireCraft: A Simulation Benchmark for Industrial DLO Manipulation
literature_claim_matrix.access: Current abstract/history and full v1 HTML accessible; release-focused searches on title, ID and authors did not verify an author-linked code release.
literature_claim_matrix.established: The latest visible arXiv entry is v1, June 16 2026, and still promises benchmark/data/tools release on acceptance. It covers insertion, clips and channels with articulated/deformable models.
literature_claim_matrix.limitation_or_distinction: No ready public package was verified; this is an access result, not proof that no code exists anywhere.
literature_claim_matrix.baseline_implication: Do not block practical setup on WireCraft or call its unpublished assets installed.

physical_design_resources.use: Physical test methods and assembly designs; simulation/task readiness not established by that page.
Fabrication and task resources; selective reuse only after exact asset/license inspection.

scope_and_limitations: This bounded review is not an exhaustive novelty search, a legal opinion or a benchmark reproduction.
Numerical literature results describe their authors' hardware/tasks; none is project cable performance.
Inaccessible methods are recorded explicitly and are not used as evidence of missing capabilities.
The one-file review ran no simulator, GPU training, benchmark policy or hardware experiment.
Publication acceptance, full-job hardware reliability and electrical/optical function are not established.
